# Levelrail

> Levelrail is a self-hosted, open-source deployment platform: an
> alternative to Heroku, Vercel, and Railway for teams who run their own
> Linux servers instead of renting one. A single Go control plane binary
> and a single Go node agent binary drive Docker's own Engine API
> directly (no SSH, no shelling out to the `docker` CLI), with metrics
> and log storage built into the core instead of a separately installed
> add-on. Push to a git repo, get a running app with TLS, logs, metrics,
> and rollback.

Apache 2.0 licensed. Source at https://github.com/glincker/levelrail.

## Tutorials

- [Getting started](https://glinr.com/levelrail/getting-started): install Levelrail and deploy your first app end to end.

## How-to guides

- [Installing](https://glinr.com/levelrail/installing): install the control plane and node agent on a Linux server.
- [Troubleshooting](https://glinr.com/levelrail/troubleshooting): fixes for the most common deploy, login, and node problems.
- [Docker](https://glinr.com/levelrail/docker): how Levelrail talks to the Docker Engine API directly.
- [Domains and ingress](https://glinr.com/levelrail/domains-and-ingress): custom domains, TLS, maintenance mode, redirects, WAF, and the embedded Caddy ingress.
- [ACME verification runbook](https://glinr.com/levelrail/acme-verification-runbook): diagnose and fix failed TLS certificate issuance.
- [Feature flags](https://glinr.com/levelrail/feature-flags): enable half-built or experimental features safely.
- [Master key rotation](https://glinr.com/levelrail/master-key-rotation): rotate the envelope-encryption master key used for secrets.
- [Migrating from Coolify, Dokploy, or CapRover](https://glinr.com/levelrail/migrating-from-coolify-dokploy-and-caprover): move an existing deployment to Levelrail.
- [Deploying from GitHub Actions](https://glinr.com/levelrail/github-actions): trigger Levelrail deploys from CI.
- [Deploying apps](https://glinr.com/levelrail/deploying-apps): app.yaml, build strategies, rolling/blue-green/recreate deploys, and rollback.
- [Managing databases](https://glinr.com/levelrail/managing-databases): managed Postgres, Redis, MySQL, MongoDB, and other engines.
- [Observability](https://glinr.com/levelrail/observability): metrics, log search, alerting, and deploy markers.
- [Multi-node](https://glinr.com/levelrail/multi-node): add servers, the WireGuard mesh, and node placement.
- [Projects and organizations](https://glinr.com/levelrail/projects-and-organizations): grouping apps and databases, environments.
- [Identity and access](https://glinr.com/levelrail/identity-and-access): users, IAM policies, API tokens, and audit logs.
- [Git integrations](https://glinr.com/levelrail/git-integrations): GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket app installs and webhook deploys.
- [Backups and storage](https://glinr.com/levelrail/backups-and-storage): scheduled backups, restore, and S3-compatible storage targets.
- [Templates and registry](https://glinr.com/levelrail/templates-and-registry): the curated one-click service catalog.
- [Screenshots](https://glinr.com/levelrail/screenshots): a visual tour of the dashboard.

## Reference

- [App spec reference](https://glinr.com/levelrail/app-spec-reference): the full app.yaml schema.
- [Feature catalog](https://glinr.com/levelrail/feature-catalog): every shipped feature, one line each.
- [CLI reference](https://glinr.com/levelrail/cli-reference): every `levelrail-cli` command and flag.
- [API reference](https://glinr.com/levelrail/api-reference): the HTTP API the dashboard, CLI, and MCP server all run on.

## Explanation

- [Architecture](https://glinr.com/levelrail/architecture): the reconciler pattern, agent transport, and why each major dependency was chosen.
- [Security overview](https://glinr.com/levelrail/security): secrets, sessions, TLS, and access control, with links to the detailed page for each.
- [Comparison](https://glinr.com/levelrail/comparison): how Levelrail differs from Coolify, Dokploy, CapRover, and Dokku.

- [Roadmap](https://glinr.com/levelrail/roadmap): phased build plan and current status.
- [Git provider integrations design proposal](https://glinr.com/levelrail/design/git-provider-integrations): a design document, not yet shipped behavior.
